title: Perfect pushforward pairing splits the counit
statement: Let p:X→Y be a scheme map [def-pc-scheme], with tensor-pullback adjunction [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction] whose unit at O_Y is invertible. For modules M,D on X and ev:M⊗D→O_X, assume p_*M is finite locally free [def-sc-finite-locally-free-sheaf] and the curry of the explicit pushed-forward pairing [def-sc-picard-cup-product-map] is invertible. Then the counit p^*p_*M→M is a split monomorphism.

source.place: final paragraph, perfect pairing and the two displayed mutually dual bases

proof.text: Finite local freeness gives an exact pairing for N=p_*M and its dual. The inverse cup transpose identifies p_*D with that dual, so the pushed pairing is an exact pairing.

Monoidal pullback preserves that exact pairing. Transport through the tensor-pullback comparison; the discrepancy between the canonical unit isomorphism and monoidal unit is an automorphism of O_X, so the explicit pulled pairing stays perfect.

The cup-product counit identity identifies this perfect pairing with ev after the two counits. For an exact pairing A⊗B→O and maps a:A→M, b:B→D respecting it, transpose the composite B⊗M→M⊗B→M⊗D→O and compose with the inverse transpose of the perfect swapped pairing. The resulting r:M→A satisfies a≫r=id by naturality of curry. Apply this to the two counits. The construction also works for zero objects and empty schemes.

proof_origin.place: Refinement of the supplied local dual-basis plan; categorical transport and stalk argument
